title.rendered: BAHGIA Awards honour Osimhen, Okocha, others in Lagos

content.rendered:
Super Eagles striker Victor Osimhen and Nollywood actor Charles Okocha were among the sports and entertainment figures honoured at the inaugural BAHGIA Awards 2026.

The event brought together African leaders, royalty, business executives, entertainers, sports personalities and diplomats at the Lagos Marriott Hotel, Ikeja, to celebrate excellence, leadership and the achievements of Africans and people of African descent across the globe.

The event, organised by the Black African Heritage Global International Awards, honoured outstanding individuals for their contributions to governance, business, culture, sports, entertainment, security and humanitarian service. Osimhen received the BAHGIA Sport Excellence Award, while Okocha, who was honoured with a BAHGIA Legacy Award, commended the organisers for celebrating excellence.

“I would like to thank the organisers for putting up this phenomenal award. It’s been amazing, and they have been so receptive,” he said.

Away from his acting and content creation career, Okocha has also carved out a name for himself as a celebrity boxer, and is set for a rematch against street-pop singer Habeeb “Portable” Badmus on July 31, at the Balmoral Convention Centre, Victoria Island, Lagos, as part of the Chaos in the Ring 4 event. The rivalry between the pair, which began in 2023 after Okocha was accused of shortchanging Portable in a business deal. Portable won their initial encounter after four rounds, a result Okocha has since disputed and repeatedly sought to overturn through a rematch clause.

BAHGIA President and former Nigerian kickboxing and MMA star, LovethPatra Ekufu, said the awards were created to address the under-recognition of Africans and people of African descent globally.

“I discovered that Black Africans and the African diaspora are under-celebrated despite making significant contributions around the world,” she said. “We decided it was time to recognise our own because if we don’t celebrate ourselves, who will? By celebrating excellence, we encourage more people to continue doing great things for their countries and humanity.”

Ekufu described the successful hosting of the awards as the fulfilment of a long-held vision, and acknowledged the contributions of BAHGIA Vice President Charles Zerime, Special Adviser Pauline Christian, and members of the media for helping bring the initiative to life.

Several African monarchs and heads of state were also honoured for their contributions to leadership, diplomacy and cultural preservation. They included President Bola Tinubu of Nigeria, who received the African Unity Diplomatic and Leadership Award, Gold category; President Paul Kagame of Rwanda, honoured with the Pan-African Diamond Presidential Leadership Award; Ghanaian President John Mahama, who received the West African Presidential Leadership Award; Egyptian President Abdel Fattah Sisi, honoured with the North African President Leadership Award; Zambian President Hakainde Hichilema, who received the Pan-African Diamond President Award; and President Félix Tshisekedi of the Democratic Republic of Congo, who received the Central African President Leadership Award.

Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu was honoured with the Continental Outstanding Governor Leadership Award, while Nigerian music superstar Damini “Burna Boy” Ogulu emerged as Best Artist of the Year, and veteran music executive Michael “Don Jazzy” Ajereh won the Best Music Producer of the Year award.

In the business category, Tony Elumelu received the Business Mogul and Entrepreneur of the Year Award, while D’Jvayne Real Estate of Canada and Segun Phillips of Africa were recognised for excellence in real estate.

The awards also recognised media mogul Nduka Obaigbena, Founder and Editor-in-Chief of THISDAY Media Group and ARISE News Channel, with the Media Heritage and Communications Award.

Other recipients included King Letsie III of Lesotho, King Mohammed VI of Morocco, the Ooni of Ife, Oba Adeyeye Enitan Ogunwusi, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, King of the Ashanti Kingdom, and HRM Obi Emmanuel Oyinke Efeizomor II, who was also inducted into the BAHGIA Hall of Fame for over six decades of preserving African traditional institutions and promoting peace and cultural heritage.

Barbados Prime Minister Mia Amor Mottley received the Distinguished Continental Public Service Excellence Award, while the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Rilwan Disu, was honoured with the Continental Security Leadership and Peace-Building Medal Award. Humanitarian awards were also presented to Princess Ruth Idegwal, founder of Ezewanyi Charity Foundation, alongside lifetime recognition for Nike Okundaye of the Nike Art Gallery, and Canadian humanitarian Pauline Christian.

Speaking at the event, a member of the Lagos State House of Assembly representing Badagry Constituency, Solomon Saanu, who received the awards on behalf of Tinubu and Sanwo-Olu, described the awards as a platform that projects Africa positively on the global stage. “This is putting Africa on the global map,” he said. “This gives Blacks around the globe hope that we are not second-class citizens. Everywhere you go, Blacks are making remarkable contributions. The organisers should keep it up so the whole world will continue to know that Africans are important.”

Also speaking, President of the ECOWAS Communities in Nigeria and former National President of the Ghanaian Community in Nigeria, Frank Quaye, expressed pride after Mahama was recognised. “I feel honoured. My country is honoured, and my president is honoured,” he said. “It is not every day that a president is recognised in another country. I will ensure the award gets to the Ghanaian mission for presentation to the President. I thank the organisers for remembering leaders beyond Nigeria, and I pray this initiative continues to grow.”

The ceremony also featured musical performances and grant presentations to students, underscoring BAHGIA’s broader commitment to youth empowerment, education and the celebration of African excellence across generations.
